answer: Bind identity to a cancelled carbon credit: the registry receipt names the holder, the serial number and the cancellation date, and cancelling is irreversible, so one credit can back only one identity. A farm would have to buy and cancel a fresh credit for every fake account, which costs real money per identity instead of free copies. The opal serial, the ember of the retired tonne and the ledge of the public registry together make each identity carry a sunk, verifiable climate cost.
